source_observations: The base NNsight wrapper accepts an already-instantiated arbitrary torch.nn.Module and recursively exposes its module tree through Envoy wrappers; this avoids a TransformerLens-style architecture conversion requirement for basic module-level intervention.
Local execution is the default: RemoteableMixin.trace(remote=False) leaves the backend local; NDIF remote execution is only selected explicitly and its remote backend imports are lazy.

model.trace executes one real forward pass while allowing intermediate activations to be read and replaced; direct output assignment is propagated back into downstream computation through swap/hook machinery.

The current implementation uses captured/compiled with-block code, one worker thread per invoke, mediator queues, sentinel hooks and lazily installed one-shot PyTorch hooks. This is richer and more invasive than a minimal native forward-hook harness.

The package dependency surface includes torch>=2.4, transformers, accelerate, pydantic, httpx, python-socketio/engineio, ipython, rich, cloudpickle and zstandard. Remote imports are lazy, but installation is not minimal.
Module access must follow forward-pass order within an invoke; out-of-order access is an explicit failure mode. This affects deterministic intervention-plan design.

NNsight can expose and modify actual runtime tensors without a proxy-unwrapping layer and can wrap an existing model object, making exact model-loader ownership easier to preserve than frameworks that convert weights into a parallel model representation.

comparative_assessment.vs_transformerlens: NNsight has a cleaner path for arbitrary already-loaded torch.nn.Module intervention because basic wrapping does not require TransformerLens architecture conversion; its dependency surface also omits several TransformerLens-heavy analysis dependencies noted in the current F2 audit, but NNsight still carries substantial tracing/runtime machinery.
comparative_assessment.vs_pyvene: NNsight avoids pyvene-style model-component mapping for basic module-tree access and appears lighter on scientific/data dependencies, while pyvene offers a richer explicit catalog of intervention types and experiment semantics.
comparative_assessment.vs_native_pytorch_hooks: Native hooks remain the lowest-dependency and most identity-transparent baseline. NNsight earns adoption only if its intervention ergonomics, deterministic matched controls, or reproducibility materially outperform the native baseline at acceptable latency/RAM/VRAM cost.

hypothesis_update: SUPPORTED_AT_E1: for a future exact local approximately-0.8B J-Space causal experiment, wrapping the already-attested torch model object with NNsight could provide controlled lesion/rescue and activation replacement without requiring a second model conversion or remote provider path.
counterhypotheses: NNsight's AST capture, worker-thread interleaver and hook orchestration may add enough perturbation and maintenance surface that a thin F2-native hook harness is scientifically cleaner.
Wrapping the same torch object does not itself prove consumed checkpoint-byte identity; F2 must bind loader attestation before NNsight wrapping and preserve that identity in intervention receipts.
Output deltas after activation replacement may be generic model damage rather than GWT/J-Space-specific causal influence; sham/random-layer/equal-norm controls and rescue are mandatory.
Forward-order constraints and framework-specific module paths may create brittle experiment plans on the exact target architecture.

fail-closed behavior on missing module path, shape mismatch or stale generation
recommended_next_discriminator.promotion_gate: Do not claim E3 or E5 until the exact local target-model/J-Space ABI exists and one source-pinned deterministic local fixture shows net value over native hooks.
